newsitem.title: USA: Empire State Building deck reopens to public.
newsitem.headline: Empire State Building deck reopens to public.

text.p: The Empire State Building's observation deck reopened on Tuesday with heavy new security measures two days after a distraught Palestinian gunman killed a tourist and wounded six others at the New York landmark.

Hundreds of visitors waited in long lines to pass through metal detectors installed after Sunday's shooting spree, when Ali Abu Kamal indiscriminately fired a semiautomatic handgun, killing Danish rock musician Christoffer Burmeister and wounding six other people before fatally shooting himself.

Many of the visitors, who included the normal mix of tour groups and schoolchildren, told reporters they were not deterred by the deadly shooting. They appeared relaxed and posed for pictures on the 86th-floor deck, which offers breath-taking views.

Authorities at the landmark building also were examining visitors' bags, using machines similar to those at airports. The extra security added "just a few minutes" to the waiting time to get to the observation deck, a trek generally slowed by waits for the elevators, a spokesman said.

Investigators who were piecing together the gunman's motives and movements before he opened fire at dusk on Sunday with a .038-calibre Beretta semiautomatic handgun said he had visited the observation deck the day before the shooting.

Authorities were speculating whether Kamal was checking for metal detectors at the popular tourist spot or perhaps had planned the shooting then but backed out. He had hired a limousine to drive him around the city and take him to the Empire State Building on Saturday, they said.

Kamal was carrying an angry two-page letter in which he lashed out at the United States, Israel, Britain and France as enemies of Palestinians and said he had been swindled out of his life savings, investigators said. They also found stacks of lottery tickets among the gunman's personal belongings.

His victims remained in hospitals. The most seriously injured, rock musician Matthew Gross, 29, of New Jersey, who suffered a gunshot wound to the head, remained in critical condition at Bellevue Hospital. Gross played in the same band, the Bush Pilots, as Burmeister, a 27-year-old guitarist.

Mario Carmona, 51, of Argentina, shot in the neck, and Jacob Schaad, 30, of Switzerland, shot in the chest, were both in serious but stable condition, the hospital said. Also in serious but stable condition at St. Vincent's Hospital were a couple from Verdun, France, and a 35-year-old Bronx man.
In the aftermath of the shooting, politicians stepped up calls for gun control that might have stopped Kamal.

New York Democratic Reps. Charles Schumer and Carolyn McCarthy held a news conference at City Hall to propose a national, government-issued handgun identification card. McCarthy became a gun control activist after her husband was killed and her son gravely wounded by a gunman on board a suburban commuter train in 1993.
Anyone who wants to buy a handgun would have to produce such a card, which would include stringent residency requirements, a spokesman for Schumer said.
Kamal, a retired college teacher who arrived in the United States on Dec. 24, bought the gun in Florida after he obtained a state identification card by checking in to a cheap motel.
